partial_case.facts: The resident first reported concerns about a retaining fence in the property's garden in August 2022. The landlord inspected it and agreed that works needed to be done. However, works were delayed. She complained to the landlord on 21 May 2024 about a lack of progress. It apologised and paid her compensation. However, it still did not carry out the repairs. She complained to us in October 2024. The landlord carried out works on the fence in July 2025. The resident reports her concerns about a retaining wall at the property to the landlord on 20 August 2022. Between 6 September 2022 and 2 September 2024, the resident raised the issue of the retaining fence with the landlord on numerous occasions. It sent people out to inspect on several occasions but took no action as it did not know if it was responsible for maintaining it. On 21 April 2024, the resident complained to the landlord about its handling of her reports that her boundary fence was dangerously in need of repair. She pointed out that she was registered blind and so found the danger posed by the fence particularly worrying. On 18 July 2024, the landlord provided its stage 1 complaint response apologising for the late complaint response and delay in carrying out necessary works, offering £350 in compensation. On 20 July 2024, the resident asked to escalate her complaint to stage 2. On 21 August 2024, the landlord issued its stage 2 complaint response, increasing its compensation offer to £700 in total. On 25 October 2024, the resident asked us to investigate, saying her back garden was unsafe so she could not use it and the landlord had failed to address the problem adequately for over 3 years.

key_reasoning_quotes.text: The landlord delayed for several years in carrying out works to the retaining fence. It has offered compensation of £650 in recognition of delay up to August 2024. However, the delay then continued until July 2025.

The primary cause for the delay was that the landlord did not know whether it was responsible for the repair of the fence. It first stated that it needed to discover whose responsibility this was in an email of 6 September 2022. It did not discover that the responsibility was its own until July 2024.

This was an appropriate sum to compensate the resident for the landlord's failure to progress repairs up until August 2024. It was in line with its and our guidance on remedies. However, as the delay continued for a further year, there was maladministration.

evidence: Resident reports and complaint chronology about the retaining fence

partial_case.facts: The landlord was Clarion Housing Association Limited and the occupancy was assured. The resident first reported concerns about a retaining fence in the property’s garden in August 2022; the landlord inspected it and agreed works were needed, but works were delayed. Between September 2022 and September 2024 the resident raised the retaining fence issue on numerous occasions, and inspections took place, but no action was taken while responsibility was unclear. The resident complained that the boundary fence was dangerously in need of repair and said she was registered blind, making the danger particularly worrying. The landlord issued stage 1 and stage 2 complaint responses, offered compensation, and said works would be carried out. The resident asked the Ombudsman to investigate in October 2024, saying her back garden was unsafe and that she wanted the landlord ordered to carry out the necessary works.

orders: Landlord to apologise in writing to the resident
Landlord to pay the resident £950 for distress, inconvenience, time and trouble caused by its handling of the resident’s reports of repairs required to a retaining fence in the garden
ground_truth_outcome.recommendation: Landlord recommended to pay the resident the £50 offered in its stage 1 response if it has not already done so

key_reasoning_quotes.text: The landlord delayed for several years in carrying out works to the retaining fence. It has offered compensation of £650 in recognition of delay up to August 2024. However, the delay then continued until July 2025.
The primary cause for the delay was that the landlord did not know whether it was responsible for the repair of the fence.
However, even after the landlord accepted responsibility for the repairs, it took a further year until July 2025 before the works were completed to the landlord’s satisfaction.
However, the landlord has relied on expert opinion in reaching its view that the works are complete and the property is safe.
Nonetheless, the delay overall was unacceptable.
However, as the delay continued for a further year, there was maladministration.
In our view, the landlord provided an appropriate level of compensation and provided reasonable redress for its complaint handling failure.
